main_text.l: PRæcipua juxta Decalogum capita percurrimus, in quibus cum Judæis

quæstionum, quod instituimus, Judaicarum merito quis desideret: sal-
tem ut loca sua singulis assignemus, quæque principaliter in rem dicenda
videntur, ne prorsus prætereamus. Ad septimum autem Decalogi præ-
ceptum, quo vetatur omne adulterium, fornicatio, & turpitudo, de Ju-
dæorum Polygamia disputandum, & Repudio, annon in legem istam
incurrant? cum enim unumquodque præceptum ita exponi debeat, ut
non modo expressum ejus caput, quod ibi memoratur, sed quæcunque
ad istam sive virtutis sive vitii speciem referuntur, eo contineri merito
arbitremur, quæritur, an sub præcepti illius septimi vi, & prohibitione
לא תנשך etiam non veniant ea quæ jam designavimus facinora, Judæis

stris in Rebuspublicis coërcent, ne id agant quod libitum sibi, aut per-

page.notes: Several Hebrew and Greek words are printed in small, blurred type and are uncertain; the Hebrew forms in the first paragraph (לא תנשך) and the Greek of the Josephus quotation are approximate. The Greek in the line "Ἀρχαιολογ." is partly illegible and has been reconstructed. The running head text "LIBER SEPTIMUS" and "CAP. VI." are set in spaced capitals. The Hebrew word for the second-to-last occurrence of pellices and the Greek words "δεσποινα" and "παλλακη" are uncertain readings.
